claims.text: Controlled bimetallic or multielement compositional variation can shift the transition-metal d-band center.
Shifting the d-band center changes the binding strength of key adsorbates under operating conditions.
Adsorbate binding governed by the d-band center determines catalytic activity.
Adsorbate binding governed by the d-band center determines catalyst stability.
A secondary metal dopant partially fills or shifts the d-band center of the host-metal matrix.
Local electronic interactions with the second metal adjust the d-band occupation of host-metal atoms.
Dopant-induced d-band adjustment improves adsorption and desorption of reaction intermediates.
Improved intermediate adsorption and desorption enhance catalytic activity.
D-band-mediated optimization of intermediate binding prevents surface deactivation.
The doped catalyst will have an onset potential approximately 50–100 mV lower than the monometallic baseline.
The doped catalyst will exhibit a higher maximum reaction rate than the monometallic baseline.
The doped or multielement catalyst will decay more slowly than the monometallic baseline.
The slower performance decay is caused by optimal adsorbate binding strength.
The effect is strongly dependent on the extent of dopant incorporation.
The effect is greatest within a specific composition range that shifts the d-band center without excessive structural reorganization.
Catalyst surfaces can undergo substantial structural or phase changes under reaction conditions.
Oxide formation or site blocking may contribute to catalytic behavior in addition to d-band modulation.
Operando XPS or XAS can be used to compare dopant-induced electronic-structure changes and adsorbate coverages.

contradictions.description: The catalysts are described as compositionally identical while also differing in the presence or relative amount of a second-metal dopant; those compositional differences make them non-identical.
The baseline is called the same catalyst composition but is also specified to contain no dopant, whereas the modified catalyst contains a dopant and therefore has a different composition.
